newsitem.title: FRANCE: Aerospatiale swings back to profit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale swings back to profit in 1996.

text.p: French state-owned Aerospatiale swung back into profit as it reported on Friday a 1996 net attributable gain of 812 million francs, compared to a prior year loss of 981 million.
The company issued a bullish forecast for the current year with profits expected to double.
"The results for the 1997 year should...see a very significant turn in the group's profitability, allowing a doubling of profits," it said in a statement with results.

Aerospatiale makes parts and assembles passenger jets for the Airbus Industrie consortium, and also manufactures tactical and strategic missiles, satellites and helicopters. The company is slated for privatisation and is in merger talks with combat jet maker Dassault Aviation.
Aerospatiale reported operating profit of 736 million francs versus 639 million a year ago, on sales of 50.9 billion francs, up from 49.2 billion.
New orders surged to 63.3 billion francs compared to 39.3 billion in 1995. The total order book stood at 129.9 billion francs versus 101.2 billion.
The company said it expects to deliver 190 planes to Airbus by the end of the 1997 year, compared to 126, which will boost turnover to 60 billion francs.

The effects of a restructuring plan started in 1995 should have their full impact this year. Also, since the beginning of this year the group has benefited from a 10 percent rise in the dollar compared to its average level last year.
World aircraft sales are denominated in dollars and Aerospatiale's major competitors are U.S. companies which have benefited from low industry costs, while its own costs are in French francs.
